summary.headline: Hy-Tech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR430 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 19.6% from 21.5%, which management blames on price-revision timing.
summary.overview:
Revenue from operations grew 13% YoY to INR430 million and PAT rose 11% to INR46 million, while EBITDA was flat at INR84 million and margin contracted about 190 bps. Management attributed the margin dip to input-cost increases from the Feb–April period whose OEM price revisions, effective 1 April, are expected to be recognised only in Q2, and a cut-off sales shift into the next quarter. This was the company's first earnings call after its 1 September listing on NSE and BSE. Management guided to ~20% revenue growth, 25–30% PAT growth and a 24–25% EBITDA margin for FY27, with capacity expansion and new-customer wins as the main drivers.</overview>

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Around 25% of revenue from USA and 7–8% from Europe; total exports about 30%. Management said exports earn roughly 10% extra margin, and a weaker rupee adds to this.

segments.name: Domestic OEM
segments.commentary: OEMs are 70–80% of business. Management expects domestic business to grow 15–20%, and domestic sales are about INR120–130 crore at present.

segments.name: Domestic distributors
segments.commentary: About 10% of business through four distributors (Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Delhi, Pune); management sees 10–30% growth potential here.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of ~20% YoY in FY27, with a 'minimum' of 20% and possibly more in the following two years.
PAT growth of 25–30% YoY; management also said bottom line would grow at least 25–30%.
EBITDA margin to be maintained at about 24–25% for FY27; management said margin rises 0.5–1% per year for 2–3 years.
Q2 FY27 expected to reflect OEM price revisions for input-cost increases, which management says will lift the quarter.
Five-year goal of about INR500 crore revenue and 50% export / 50% domestic mix; capacity target of 70 lakh fittings per month within about three years.
Management said the business could double in three to four years and it cited a multi-year 25–30% growth trajectory.
capex_capacity: Current installed capacity of about 35 lakh fittings per month across six plants (two in Shirwal, one each in Pithampur (two), Nashik and Thane); target 70 lakh per month.

Capex of INR30 crore allotted for FY27 for rotary transfer machines (two installed, four more planned), to be implemented within about one year; management said this adds about INR100 crore of business.

Board approved purchase of 6.5 acres of land for a future plant, with acquisition in 3–4 months; plant investment estimated at INR350–500 crore, with a 2–3 year horizon and roughly two times the productivity of current plants.
Utilisation of forging and hydraulic fitting capacity at 60–70%; forging capacity 15–20% above requirement after two mechanical presses (Shirwal, Nashik).
Management said existing infrastructure allows scaling from 200 to 300 without new buildings. Current land is about 8 acres (3,20,000 sq ft).
demand_pricing: Management says price increases are passed through to OEMs under long-term understandings, with compensation typically in 3–6 months; Q1 margin was hit by the timing gap.
Competitive position: Parker fittings priced about 2x Hy-Tech's; management says there is no Chinese competition in its products; second domestic competitor has less than half Hy-Tech's turnover.
Total addressable market cited as INR40,000 crore globally (USA INR20,000 crore, Europe INR10,000 crore, India INR2,000 crore, other INR8,000 crore). Management says it holds about 10% of India.
Sany (Chinese excavator maker) approached Hy-Tech to indigenise its fittings supply; management also expects tenders and government-linked OEMs to be added.
Management said no single customer exceeds 15% of revenue; about 170 direct customers. Pipeline includes Tata Hitachi, Sany and Fluidconnecto added at bauma.
Stainless steel fittings for data centres and oil & gas: range developed over 1.5–2 years; management expects revenue in FY28–FY29, with no current customer discussions specified.

qa_highlights.question: What cut the margin and what FY27 EBITDA margin should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 24–25% EBITDA margin for FY27 and said the Q1 drop reflected input-cost increases and an OEM price revision effective 1 April that will be recognised in Q2. Management also said PAT should grow 25–30%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue growth guidance for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue to grow at least 20% YoY, with PAT growing 25–30% per year. Management said it has no formal order book, only annual schedules and contract prices from OEMs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and capacity expansion plan?
qa_highlights.answer: INR30 crore capex this year, to be implemented within one year. A 6.5-acre land purchase is planned for a future plant estimated at INR350–500 crore in 2–3 years; a US subsidiary is also being set up.

qa_highlights.question: How is the US business and export mix planned?
qa_highlights.answer: US is about 25% of revenue and management intends to hold it there. Total export target is 50% in five years, spread across Europe, Australia, New Zealand and Dubai.

qa_highlights.question: Why did new SKU additions fall from about 2,206 in FY24 to about 880 in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SKU additions depend on OEM RFQs for new equipment, not on cost or a deliberate slowdown.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said absolute employee cost rose in line with the top line, and that a cut-off sales shift into Q2 makes the ratio about 12% of sales.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 must show the OEM price pass-through and margin recovery toward 24–25%; the Q1 margin fall (19.6% vs 21.5%) is the key open point.
Dependence on US exports (about 25% of revenue) under tariff and geopolitical risk; management says it will cap US share.
Execution of the INR30 crore capex and the 6.5-acre plant (INR350–500 crore), including land acquisition in 3–4 months and government approvals.
Railway (IRIS), defence (DRDO) and shipyard (Cochin Shipyard, Mazagon Dock) orders are at registration stage; first revenue is uncertain, possibly after 5–6 months.
Slowing new SKU additions (FY24 about 2,206 to FY26 about 880) and R&D at about 1% of revenue.
Fixed-asset (PPE) figures were disputed on the call: INR641 million (FY25) vs INR594.95 million (FY26). The company attributed the difference to depreciation and CWIP.
